submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad head: ordinary prose and code often crosses the active line weakly (about 0.75-1.3; 8 of 20 varied plain sentences crossed), so predict ordinary text active-weak; it is strong (above about 1.5) on the token right after a '/' joining two numbers or a number and unit ('5/8', '24/7', '12/25/1990', '2/6*', 'km/h'), attending almost entirely to the '/', and moderately to strongly on the word that closes a frame opened a few tokens back that it attends to ('to' after 'from X', 'to'/'for' after 'it is/make it ADJ', 'on' after 'impact/effect ... have/has'). Predicted inactive (below 0.25 x max): a whole text that is one single-token word plus a period (exactly 2 tokens, e.g. 'Hello.', 'Yes.'), or only a comma-and-space list of 5-7 distinct plain integers 0-99 (9-13 tokens, no other words); outside these classes, multi-token words plus a period ('Seriously.'), '!' endings ('Help!'), and integer lists of 8 or more items can cross.
